datasets.description_md: eDNA metabarcoding survey of vertebrates from water samples collected during the October 2022 CalCOFI cruise. Water filters from CalCOFI/GEMCAP stations off Southern California were run through one or two molecular assays: a mitochondrial D-loop assay (cetacean detections, incl. Delphinus and Megaptera novaeangliae) and a 12S rRNA "MiFish" assay (fish detections). Published as an intercalibration exercise (source datasetID "CalCOFI_Intercal") on GBIF/OBIS, linked to Patin et al. 2026 (Methods in Ecology and Evolution, https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210x.70370). Sequence read counts are a semi-quantitative signal of PCR-amplified DNA, not abundance, and are not comparable between assays. Published as detections only: edna_presence = 1 and the read counts. The source archive holds positive detections only, so the absence of a row for a filter and taxon is not a non-detection for this dataset (a filter or assay run with no detection is simply missing, and absence cannot be inferred); this differs from sio_cetacean-edna, where 0 means not detected in a sequenced sample.

The dataset covers twelve quarterly CalCOFI cruises and spans January 1994 to October 1996. At roughly half the stations sampled on each cruise, water was collected at multiple depths using closing bottles on a CTD rosette; chlorophyll from each bottle was retained on a GF/F glass-fiber filter and measured fluorometrically, while an additional combined sample from the shallowest ten bottles (surface to about 100 m) was filtered through an 8 μm membrane filter to isolate the larger size fraction. This dataset supports study of organic carbon cycling in coastal and open ocean waters of the California Current, for researchers studying carbon dynamics in the California Current ecosystem. The dataset covers CalCOFI and California Current Ecosystem Long-Term Ecological Research (CCE-LTER) stations off Southern and Central California and spans 2014 to 2019, archived across two NCBI BioProject deposits (PRJNA555783 for 2014-2016 and PRJNA665326 for 2017-2019, which also includes some 2014-2016 samples and extends metatranscriptomics data through 2020). Whole water samples were filtered onto 0.2 micrometer filters to capture DNA and RNA at four depths, 10 meters, the subsurface chlorophyll maximum layer, 170 meters, and 515 meters, then sequenced using 16S V4 metabarcoding to identify bacteria and archaea, and 18S V4 and V9 metabarcoding to identify eukaryotic plankton such as protists and small zooplankton. The same archived deposits also include total mRNA sequencing (metatranscriptomics) data from these samples. This dataset supports research identifying amplicon sequence variants (ASVs), a method for distinguishing microbial and plankton taxa at high resolution, and characterizing community structure and diversity, and is intended for researchers studying plankton and microbial ecology in the California Current.

The dataset covers the southern California Current and spans 2022 to ongoing, since the Imaging FlowCytobot (IFCB) was first deployed on CalCOFI cruises. Discrete water samples are collected from 10 meters and the chlorophyll maximum depth during CTD casts and imaged using the IFCB, an automated flow cytometer that combines flow cytometry and video technology to photograph individual suspended particles. Images are processed to estimate particle volume and identity, along with geolocation, sampling conditions, and instrument metadata, allowing estimates of plankton abundance, biovolume, and carbon content. This dataset supports research on fine-scale plankton community composition and spatial and temporal variability, and is intended for researchers studying phytoplankton ecology in the California Current.

The dataset covers Monterey Bay, California, and spans 1954 to 1968, a subset of Hopkins Marine Station's broader weekly CalCOFI sampling program that ran from March 1951 through June 1974. Data were collected through weekly field sampling and later transcribed from the original raw and aggregated records held at the Hopkins Marine Station library. This dataset supports historical research on phytoplankton community composition in Monterey Bay, extending oceanographic observations in the Northeast Pacific decades into the past, and is intended for researchers studying long-term or historical trends in phytoplankton populations and California Current oceanography. This dataset covers only a subset of the full 1951 to 1974 Hopkins Marine Station sampling period; Moss Landing Marine Laboratories took over the Monterey Bay sampling program in July 1974, continuing similar sampling until it appears to have ended in 1979.

holdings.description_md: CalCOFI Additional CTD Hydrographic Cast Data contains temperature, salinity, and dissolved oxygen measurements from CTD (conductivity-temperature-depth) casts taken during California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations (CalCOFI) cruises and related NOAA cruises. The dataset covers primarily the CalCOFI station grid off Southern and Central California, with related NOAA cruises extending north into the Pacific Northwest and offshore, and spans 2002 to 2014. A CTD instrument is lowered through the water column at each station, recording temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen concentration and saturation, and depth to about 1,000 meters. Most oxygen and salinity values here have not been calibrated against water samples, so users needing calibrated hydrographic data should use the SIO CalCOFI CTD cast and bottle datasets instead, which are corrected using bottle sample comparisons. This dataset is best used as a supplementary record of additional NOAA CTD casts outside the primary SIO hydrographic time series.
